Computes the exact Euclidean distance from a query point to the boundary of an axis-aligned rectangle centered at the origin [S1, unofficial].

The code snippet in Source [S1] defines a function `sdRect` that computes the signed distance to an axis-aligned rectangle centered at the origin. The formula `length(max(dv, 0.0)) + min(max(dv.x, dv.y), 0.0)` is the standard analytical solution for the exact Euclidean signed distance from a point to an AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box). The claim specifies 'Euclidean distance from a query point to the boundary', which corresponds to the absolute value of this signed distance (or the signed distance itself, which indicates position relative to the boundary). Since the code implements the exact mathematical formula for this distance, the evidence supports the claim.

where $|p_x|$ and $|p_y|$ apply the absolute value component-wise [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that in the context of the provided evidence, the notation $|p_x|$ and $|p_y|$ applies the absolute value component-wise. The evidence includes the GLSL function `sdRect` which defines `vec2 dv = abs(p) - hsize;`. In GLSL, the `abs()` function applied to a vector (`vec2`) operates component-wise. Therefore, `dv.x` corresponds to `abs(p.x) - hsize.x` and `dv.y` corresponds to `abs(p.y) - hsize.y`. The claim accurately describes this component-wise application of the absolute value operation on the components of vector `p`.

In GLSL, `max(vec2, float)` is a standard vectorized operation that compares each component of the vector `dv` against the scalar `0.0` and returns the maximum of the two for each component. This matches the description 'applies the maximum operator to each component with 0'. The claim also states that `||.||` is the Euclidean length, which corresponds to the `length()` function used in the code `length(max(dv, 0.0))`. This captures the distance to the closest edge when the point is inside the rectangle [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the code captures the distance to the closest edge when the point is inside the rectangle. The provided code `sdRect` calculates the signed distance to an axis-aligned rectangle. When a point `p` is inside the rectangle, `dv` (which is `abs(p) - hsize`) will have negative components. `max(dv, 0.0)` will be zero, so the first term `length(max(dv, 0.0))` is 0. The second term `min(max(dv.x, dv.y), 0.0)` will be negative, representing the negative distance to the closest edge (since `dv.x` and `dv.y` are negative, their max is the one closer to zero, i.e., the smallest magnitude negative value, and taking the min with 0 keeps it negative). Thus, the function returns the negative distance to the closest edge, which correctly 'captures' this distance (with a sign indicating inside/outside). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.
